title: R001 · Class I / Level A · Prevention of heart failure
text: Strict blood pressure control (systolic blood pressure target <130 mmHg) is recommended in patients with hypertension or stage B HF to reduce the risk of HF.

title: R002 · Class I / Level A · Prevention of heart failure
text: An SGLT2-I is recommended in patients with T2DM at risk of HF (multiple ASCVD risk factors or established ASCVD) to reduce the risk of HF and CV death.

title: R003 · Class I / Level A · Prevention of heart failure
text: An SGLT2-I is recommended in patients with T2DM and CKD to reduce the risk of HF or CV death.

title: R004 · Class I / Level A · Prevention of heart failure
text: Finerenone is recommended in patients with T2DM and CKD to reduce the risk of HF.

title: R005 · Class I / Level C · Prevention of heart failure
text: Counselling on healthy lifestyle choices including maintaining a healthy weight, consuming a well-balanced diet, avoiding sedentary behaviour, abstaining from smoking and heavy alcohol consumption as well as counselling against the use of drugs such as cocaine, amphetamines, and anabolic steroids is recommended for all patients with stage A or B HF to reduce the risk of HF progression.

title: R006 · Class IIa / Level A · Prevention of heart failure
text: Treatment with a statin should be considered in people at high risk of, or with established ASCVD, to reduce the risk of HF.

title: R007 · Class IIa / Level A · Prevention of heart failure
text: A GLP-1 RA should be considered in patients with T2DM and at least one other additional CV risk factor to reduce the risk of HF or CV death.

title: R008 · Class I / Level A · Stage B heart failure & LV dysfunction
text: An ACE-I or ARB (if intolerant to ACE-I) is recommended in patients with stage B HF and LVEF ≤ 40% to reduce the risk of HFH and death.

title: R009 · Class I / Level B1 · Stage B heart failure & LV dysfunction
text: A beta-blocker is recommended in patients with stage B HF and LVEF <50% to reduce the risk of HFH or death.

title: R010 · Class I / Level B1 · Stage B heart failure & LV dysfunction
text: Eplerenone is recommended in patients with LVEF ≤ 40% after myocardial infarction with signs of HF or diabetes to reduce the risk of HFH and death.

title: R011 · Class I / Level C · Diagnostic investigations in suspected HF
text: In patients with suspected HF, the following laboratory tests are recommended when screening for comorbidities: full blood count, kidney function (eGFR and UACR), electrolytes, liver function, thyroid function, HbA1c, lipids, and iron status (TSAT and ferritin).

title: R012 · Class I / Level C · Diagnostic investigations in suspected HF
text: Natriuretic peptide measurement is recommended in patients with suspected HF (interpreted in relation to patient age, obesity, and other factors known to affect natriuretic peptide level).

title: R013 · Class I / Level C · Diagnostic investigations in suspected HF
text: A 12-lead ECG is recommended in patients with suspected HF.

title: R014 · Class I / Level C · Diagnostic investigations in suspected HF
text: Chest radiography (X-ray) is recommended in patients with suspected HF.

title: R015 · Class I / Level C · Diagnostic investigations in suspected HF
text: Transthoracic echocardiogram is recommended in patients with suspected HF to confirm the diagnosis, differentiate between HF phenotypes and aid in identifying the underlying aetiology of HF.

title: R016 · Class I / Level C · Specialized diagnostic investigations (aetiology)
text: Contrast-enhanced CMR is recommended in patients with suspected cardiomyopathy, or where the underlying aetiology of HF is uncertain if further characterization is likely to add value to patient care.

title: R017 · Class I / Level B · Specialized diagnostic investigations (aetiology)
text: Initial diagnostic testing with serum and urine immunofixation, serum free light chains assay, and DPD/PYP/HMDP bone scintigraphy is recommended in patients with HF and a suspicion of cardiac amyloidosis.

title: R018 · Class I / Level C · Specialized diagnostic investigations (aetiology)
text: Genetic testing is recommended in patients fulfilling diagnostic criteria for cardiomyopathy in cases where it enables diagnosis, prognostication, therapeutic stratification, or reproductive management of the patient, or where it enables cascade genetic evaluation of their relatives who would otherwise be enrolled into long-term surveillance.

title: R019 · Class I / Level C · Specialized diagnostic investigations (aetiology)
text: Invasive coronary angiography is recommended in patients with HF, angina, and high probability of obstructive CAD who are potential candidates for revascularization.

title: R020 · Class IIa / Level C · Specialized diagnostic investigations (aetiology)
text: 18F-FDG-PET scanning should be considered for the diagnostic work-up in patients with cardiomyopathy in whom cardiac sarcoidosis is suspected.

title: R021 · Class IIa / Level C · Specialized diagnostic investigations (aetiology)
text: Endomyocardial biopsy should be considered to aid in diagnosis and management in patients with rapidly progressive HF despite standard therapy or when the results of other clinical investigations suggest myocardial inflammation, infiltration, or storage that cannot be identified by other means.

title: R022 · Class IIa / Level C · Specialized diagnostic investigations (aetiology)
text: Right heart catheterization should be considered in patients where HF is thought to be due to constrictive pericarditis or congenital heart disease.

title: R023 · Class IIb / Level C · Specialized diagnostic investigations (aetiology)
text: Right heart catheterization may be considered in selected patients with suspected HFpEF or structural heart disease to confirm the diagnosis, or when clinical examination and non-invasive testing are insufficient to understand the haemodynamic state.

title: R024 · Class IIa / Level C · Specialized diagnostic investigations (aetiology)
text: Invasive coronary angiography should be considered in patients with HFrEF and high pre-test likelihood of obstructive CAD, taking into account the risk-to-benefit ratio of the procedures and potential revascularization strategies.

title: R025 · Class IIa / Level C · Specialized diagnostic investigations (aetiology)
text: CTCA should be considered in patients with HFrEF and low-moderate pre-test likelihood of obstructive CAD.

title: R026 · Class IIa / Level C · Specialized diagnostic investigations (aetiology)
text: Review of the proportion of RV pacing should be considered in all patients with CIED and de novo or worsening HFrEF.

title: R027 · Class IIb / Level C · Specialized diagnostic investigations (aetiology)
text: Electrical cardioversion as a diagnostic tool may be considered in patients with persistent AF where there is uncertainty about the value of sinus rhythm restoration on symptoms or to assess improvement in left ventricular function.

title: R028 · Class I / Level A · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: An SGLT2-I (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin) is recommended in patients with symptomatic HF independent of LVEF to reduce the risk of HFH or CV death.

title: R029 · Class I / Level A · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: An MRA (sMRA for HFrEF and sMRA/nsMRA for HFpEF) is recommended in patients with symptomatic HF independent of LVEF to reduce the risk of HFH or CV death.

title: R030 · Class I / Level A · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: Dynamic individualized dosing of loop diuretics according to volume status is recommended in patients with HF and signs and/ or symptoms of congestion to alleviate HF symptoms, improve exercise capacity, and reduce the risk of HFH.

title: R031 · Class I / Level C · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: Uptitration of FMT at least every 1–2 weeks in patients with HF, guided by symptoms, vital signs, and laboratory findings, to achieve optimal target doses shown to be efficacious in RCTs is recommended to reduce the risk of HFH or death.

title: R032 · Class I / Level C · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: Continuation of FMT at the highest tolerated doses is recommended in all patients with HF, including those who become asymptomatic or with LVEF improvement, in order to reduce the risk of HFH and death.

title: R033 · Class I / Level A · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: A beta-blocker is recommended in stable patients with symptomatic HFrEF to reduce the risk of HFH and death.

title: R034 · Class I / Level A · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: An ACE-I or ARNI is recommended in patients with symptomatic HFrEF to reduce the risk of HFH and death.

title: R035 · Class I / Level B1 · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: Switching from an ACE-I or ARB to an ARNI is recommended in patients with symptomatic HFrEF to reduce the risk of HFH and death.

title: R036 · Class I / Level A · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: An ARB is recommended in patients with symptomatic HFrEF to reduce the risk of HFH and CV death if they are unable to tolerate an ACE-I or ARNI.

title: R037 · Class IIa / Level B1 · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: A cardiac glycoside (digoxin or digitoxin) should be considered in patients with symptomatic HFrEF with LVEF ≤40%, despite optimal FMT, to reduce the risk of HFH.

title: R038 · Class IIa / Level B1 · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: Ivabradine should be considered for patients with symptomatic HFrEF, LVEF ≤ 35%, in sinus rhythm, resting heart rate >70 b.p.m., on the highest tolerated ACE-I/ARNI, MRA, SGLT2-I, and beta-blockers to reduce the risk of HFH or CV death.

title: R039 · Class IIa / Level C · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: Ivabradine should be considered in patients with symptomatic HFrEF, LVEF ≤ 35%, in sinus rhythm, who are unable to tolerate a beta-blocker, on the highest tolerated ACE-I/ARNI and MRA to reduce the risk of HFH or CV death.

title: R040 · Class IIa / Level B2 · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: Hydralazine and isosorbide dinitrate should be considered in self-identified black patients with symptomatic HFrEF with LVEF ≤ 40% on top of optimal FMT to reduce the risk of HFH and death.

title: R041 · Class IIb / Level C · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: Hydralazine and isosorbide dinitrate may be considered in patients with symptomatic HFrEF with LVEF ≤ 40% who cannot tolerate ARNI, ACE-I, or ARB to reduce the risk of HFH and death.

title: R042 · Class IIb / Level B1 · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: Vericiguat may be considered in patients with symptomatic HFrEF and LVEF <45% despite treatment with optimal FMT to reduce the risk of HFH and CV death.

title: R043 · Class IIb / Level C · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: Gradual discontinuation of FMT under frequent clinical, laboratory, and imaging surveillance may be considered in highly selected patients who are asymptomatic with complete normalization of LV function and volume as well as natriuretic peptide levels after specific treatment of reversible causes of HF, in order to accommodate patient preference.

title: R044 · Class IIb / Level C · Pharmacological management of chronic HF
text: ACE-I/ARB/ARNI may be considered in patients with symptomatic HFpEF to reduce the risk of HFH.

title: R045 · Class I / Level A · ICD implantation
text: An ICD is recommended in patients who have recovered from a ventricular arrhythmia causing haemodynamic instability (secondary prevention), and who are expected to survive for >1 year with good functional status, in the absence of reversible causes, or unless the ventricular arrhythmia has occurred <48 h after an MI, to reduce the risk of sudden death and all-cause death.

title: R046 · Class I / Level B1 · ICD implantation
text: An ICD is recommended in patients with symptomatic HFrEF (NYHA class II/III) of an ischaemic aetiology (unless they have had an MI in the prior 40 days), and an LVEF ≤35% despite ≥3 months of optimal FMT, provided they are expected to survive longer than 1 year with good functional status, to reduce the risk of sudden death and all-cause death.

title: R047 · Class IIa / Level B1 · ICD implantation
text: An ICD should be considered in patients with symptomatic HFrEF (NYHA class II/III) of a non-ischaemic aetiology, and an LVEF ≤35% despite ≥3 months of optimal FMT, provided they are expected to survive longer than 1 year with good functional status, to reduce the risk of sudden death and all-cause death.

title: R048 · Class IIa / Level C · ICD implantation
text: Prior to generator replacement for CIEDs, a shared decision-making process between the patient and a cardiologist experienced in CIEDs and HF should be considered to ensure that the balance between risks and benefits still favour a CIED.

title: R049 · Class IIb / Level C · ICD implantation
text: A wearable cardioverter-defibrillator may be considered in patients with HF who are at risk of sudden cardiac death for a limited period in order to increase survival as a bridge to decision for permanent ICD implantation or while listed for heart transplantation.

title: R050 · Class III / Level B1 · ICD implantation
text: ICD implantation for primary prevention is not recommended within 40 days of an MI as implantation during this period does not improve prognosis.

title: R051 · Class III / Level C · ICD implantation
text: ICD implantation is not recommended in patients in NYHA class IV with severe symptoms refractory to pharmacological therapy unless they are candidates for CRT, a ventricular assist device, or heart transplantation.

title: R052 · Class I / Level A · Cardiac resynchronization therapy
text: CRT is recommended in patients with symptomatic HFrEF, LVEF ≤ 35%, despite optimal FMT, in SR with LBBB and QRS duration ≥ 150 ms in order to improve symptoms and reduce the risk of hospitalizations and death.

title: R053 · Class IIa / Level B1 · Cardiac resynchronization therapy
text: An upgrade to CRT should be considered in patients with an LVEF ≤ 35% who have received a conventional pacemaker or an ICD and subsequently develop worsening HF despite optimal FMT and who have a significant proportion of RV pacing in order to reduce the risk of HFH or death.

title: R054 · Class IIa / Level B1 · Cardiac resynchronization therapy
text: CRT, rather than RV pacing, should be considered in patients with HFrEF regardless of NYHA class or QRS width who have an indication for ventricular pacing for high-degree AV block in order to reduce the risk of HFH and death.

title: R055 · Class IIa / Level C · Cardiac resynchronization therapy
text: CRT should be considered in patients with symptomatic HFrEF, LVEF ≤ 35%, despite optimal FMT, who are in SR with non-LBBB QRS morphology and QRS duration ≥ 150 ms in order to improve symptoms and reduce morbidity and death.

title: R056 · Class IIa / Level C · Cardiac resynchronization therapy
text: CRT should be considered in patients with symptomatic HFrEF, LVEF ≤ 35%, despite optimal FMT, who are in SR with LBBB QRS morphology and QRS duration of 130–149 ms in order to improve symptoms and reduce morbidity and death.

title: R057 · Class IIb / Level C · Cardiac resynchronization therapy
text: CRT may be considered in patients with symptomatic HFrEF, LVEF ≤ 35%, despite optimal FMT, who are in SR with non-LBBB QRS morphology and QRS duration of 130–149 ms in order to improve symptoms and reduce morbidity and death.

title: R058 · Class IIb / Level C · Cardiac resynchronization therapy
text: Initiation of FMT and planning for CRT implantation may be considered simultaneously in patients with symptomatic HFrEF, an LBBB with QRS ≥150 ms, and LVEF ≤35%, to improve symptoms and reduce morbidity and death, although reassessment of LVEF should be conducted prior to CRT implantation.

title: R059 · Class III / Level A · Cardiac resynchronization therapy
text: CRT is not recommended in patients with a QRS duration <130 ms who do not have an indication for pacing due to high-degree AV block.

title: R060 · Class I / Level C · Pre-/early post-discharge follow-up after DHF
text: Careful evaluation before discharge is recommended in patients hospitalized for DHF to exclude persistent signs of congestion.

title: R061 · Class I / Level B2 · Pre-/early post-discharge follow-up after DHF
text: An intensive strategy of rapid initiation and uptitration of FMT before discharge and during frequent follow-up visits in the first 6 weeks following an HFH is recommended to reduce the risk of HF rehospitalization or death.

title: R062 · Class I / Level C · Immediate & intermediate treatment of decompensated HF
text: Oxygen is recommended in patients with SpO2 <90% or PaO2 <60 mmHg to correct hypoxaemia.

title: R063 · Class I / Level C · Immediate & intermediate treatment of decompensated HF
text: Intubation is recommended in patients with DHF and persistent and progressive respiratory failure despite oxygen administration or non-invasive ventilation to correct hypoxaemia.

title: R064 · Class IIa / Level B2 · Immediate & intermediate treatment of decompensated HF
text: Non-invasive positive pressure ventilation should be considered in patients with respiratory distress (respiratory rate >25 breaths/min, SpO2 <90%) and started as soon as possible in order to decrease respiratory distress and reduce the risk of endotracheal intubation.

title: R065 · Class I / Level A · Immediate & intermediate treatment of decompensated HF
text: Intravenous loop diuretics are recommended for all patients with DHF admitted with fluid overload to improve symptoms.

title: R066 · Class IIa / Level B1 · Immediate & intermediate treatment of decompensated HF
text: The addition of short-term intravenous acetazolamide or oral hydrochlorothiazide should be considered in patients with fluid overload previously treated with loop diuretics, to reduce congestion.

title: R067 · Class IIb / Level B1 · Immediate & intermediate treatment of decompensated HF
text: Urinary Na⁺-guided diuretic therapy may be considered during the first days of treatment of patients with DHF to improve natriuresis and diuresis.

title: R068 · Class I / Level B1 · Immediate & intermediate treatment of decompensated HF
text: In-hospital initiation of SGLT2-I is recommended in patients with DHF after initial stabilization to improve QoL and congestion symptoms and reduce the risk of HFH.

title: R069 · Class IIb / Level C · Immediate & intermediate treatment of decompensated HF
text: Intravenous vasodilators may be considered as initial therapy in patients with DHF and systolic blood pressure >110 mmHg to improve symptoms and reduce congestion.

title: R070 · Class IIb / Level C · Immediate & intermediate treatment of decompensated HF
text: Inotropic agents may be considered in patients with systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg and evidence of hypoperfusion who do not respond to standard treatment, including fluid challenge, to improve perfusion.

title: R071 · Class IIb / Level C · Immediate & intermediate treatment of decompensated HF
text: Vasopressors, preferably norepinephrine, may be considered in patients with cardiogenic shock to increase blood pressure and vital organ perfusion.

title: R072 · Class III / Level C · Immediate & intermediate treatment of decompensated HF
text: Routine use of opiates is not recommended in patients with DHF unless severe/intractable pain or anxiety, due to risk of harm.

title: R073 · Class I / Level C · Temporary MCS in cardiogenic shock
text: A multidisciplinary Shock Team is recommended in potential candidates for temporary MCS to guide the device selection (modality and type) based on patient and HF characteristics.

title: R074 · Class IIa / Level B1 · Temporary MCS in cardiogenic shock
text: Temporary MCS with a microaxial flow pump should be considered in selected patients with cardiogenic shock caused by ST-elevation MI with left ventricular systolic dysfunction and no risk of hypoxic brain injury in order to reduce the risk of death.

title: R075 · Class III / Level B1 · Temporary MCS in cardiogenic shock
text: Temporary MCS is not recommended in unselected patients with cardiogenic shock caused by acute MI, due to risk of harm.

title: R076 · Class III / Level B1 · Temporary MCS in cardiogenic shock
text: IABP is not recommended in unselected patients with cardiogenic shock, due to the lack of effect.

title: R077 · Class IIa / Level C · Temporary MCS in cardiogenic shock
text: Temporary MCS should be considered in patients with mechanical complications related to MI as a bridge to definitive treatment.

title: R078 · Class IIa / Level C · Temporary MCS in cardiogenic shock
text: Temporary MCS should be considered in selected patients with HF-related haemodynamic instability as a BTR, BTD, BTB, BTC, or BTT.

title: R079 · Class I / Level A · Diagnosis & evaluation of advanced HF
text: Early consultation with an advanced HF centre is recommended in patients with advanced HF or at risk of advanced HF, who are motivated and do not have absolute contraindications for heart transplantation or durable MCS, in order to evaluate candidacy.

title: R080 · Class I / Level C · Diagnosis & evaluation of advanced HF
text: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing is recommended in patients with advanced HF, as part of the evaluation for heart transplantation and durable MCS.

title: R081 · Class I / Level C · Diagnosis & evaluation of advanced HF
text: Right heart catheterization is recommended in patients with advanced HF, as part of the evaluation for heart transplantation and durable MCS.

title: R082 · Class IIa / Level C · Medical management of advanced HF
text: Down-titration or discontinuation of beta-blockers or ivabradine should be considered in selected patients with advanced HFrEF and evidence of organ hypoperfusion, despite initial treatment, to increase cardiac output and improve symptoms.

title: R083 · Class IIa / Level C · Medical management of advanced HF
text: Continuous inotropes should be considered in patients with advanced HFrEF, low cardiac output, and evidence of hypoperfusion or end-organ dysfunction, as BTD, BTT or as bridge to durable MCS, to increase cardiac output and improve symptoms.

title: R084 · Class IIa / Level C · Medical management of advanced HF
text: Kidney replacement therapy should be considered in patients with refractory volume overload and end-stage kidney failure to improve symptoms.

title: R085 · Class IIb / Level C · Medical management of advanced HF
text: Ultrafiltration may be considered in patients with refractory volume overload unresponsive to escalation of diuretic therapy to reduce the risk of rehospitalization.

title: R086 · Class I / Level C · Durable MCS in advanced HF
text: Durable MCS (LVAD) is recommended in selected patients with advanced HFrEF, despite FMT and GDIT, as BTT, BTC, BTR, or as destination therapy to improve symptoms and reduce the risk of death.

title: R087 · Class IIa / Level C · Durable MCS in advanced HF
text: Histopathological examination of explanted heart tissue from LVAD or heart transplantation surgery should be considered in patients with non-ischaemic HF to identify an aetiological diagnosis that may be treatable or facilitate family screening.

title: R088 · Class I / Level C · Heart transplantation
text: Heart transplantation is recommended in selected patients with advanced HF refractory to FMT and GDIT, and without contraindications, to improve QoL and survival.

title: R089 · Class I / Level A · Atrial fibrillation in HF
text: Oral anticoagulation is recommended in patients with clinical AF at elevated thromboembolic risk, as determined by CHA₂DS₂-VA score, to prevent ischaemic stroke and thromboembolism.

title: R090 · Class I / Level B1 · Atrial fibrillation in HF
text: DOACs are recommended in preference to VKAs in patients with HF to prevent stroke and thromboembolism.

title: R091 · Class I / Level C · Atrial fibrillation in HF
text: Beta-blockers are recommended in stable patients with HFrEF and AF as first-line therapy for short- and long-term rate control.

title: R092 · Class IIa / Level C · Atrial fibrillation in HF
text: Digoxin should be considered in stable patients with HFrEF and AF when the ventricular rate remains high despite beta-blockers, or when beta-blockers are contraindicated/not tolerated, in order to obtain short- and long-term rate control.

title: R093 · Class IIa / Level B1 · Atrial fibrillation in HF
text: Atrioventricular node ablation combined with CRT should be considered in patients with severely symptomatic permanent AF and poor rate control despite medical therapy and at least one HFH to reduce symptoms, physical limitations, recurrent HFH, and death.

title: R094 · Class IIb / Level C · Atrial fibrillation in HF
text: Intravenous amiodarone or digoxin may be considered in haemodynamically unstable patients with HFrEF and AF to stabilize the patient and achieve acute control of heart rate.

title: R095 · Class I / Level C · Atrial fibrillation in HF
text: Urgent cardioversion is recommended in the setting of DHF in patients presenting with rapid ventricular rates and haemodynamic instability to restore sinus rhythm.

title: R096 · Class IIa / Level C · Atrial fibrillation in HF
text: Catheter ablation for AF should be considered in selected patients with symptomatic AF and HFrEF to improve QoL and reduce the risk of HFH or death.

title: R097 · Class I / Level C · Revascularization in chronic coronary syndrome
text: Coronary revascularization is recommended in patients with HF, obstructive CAD, and persistent angina, despite FMT for HF and antianginal drugs, to relieve symptoms.

title: R098 · Class IIa / Level B1 · Revascularization in chronic coronary syndrome
text: If revascularization is planned after assessment by a Heart Team, CABG should be considered as the preferred revascularization strategy, in patients with LVEF ≤ 35% and multivessel CAD suitable for surgery, to improve long-term survival.

title: R099 · Class I / Level B1 · Valvular heart disease in HF
text: Aortic valve intervention, SAVR or TAVI, is recommended in patients with severe aortic stenosis and HF to improve symptoms and reduce the risk of death.

title: R100 · Class I / Level B1 · Valvular heart disease in HF
text: Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is recommended in haemodynamically stable, symptomatic patients with HFrEF and persistent severe secondary mitral regurgitation despite optimized FMT and CRT if indicated, who fulfil specific clinical and echocardiographic criteria, in order to reduce the risk of HFH and improve

title: R101 · Class IIb / Level C · Valvular heart disease in HF
text: Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair may be considered in selected symptomatic patients with HFrEF and persistent severe secondary mitral regurgitation despite optimized FMT and CRT if indicated (after excluding the option of LVAD or heart transplantation) who do not fulfil the specific clinical and echocardiographic criteria, in order to reduce the risk of HFH and improve QoL.

title: R102 · Class IIa / Level B1 · Obesity in HF
text: Semaglutide or tirzepatide should be considered for patients with symptomatic HF, LVEF ≥ 45%, and BMI ≥ 30 kg/m², regardless of diabetes status, to reduce body weight, and improve exercise capacity and QoL.

title: R103 · Class IIb / Level C · Obesity in HF
text: Bariatric surgery may be considered in obese patients with HF and a BMI ≥ 35 kg/m² to reduce body weight when repetitive and structured lifestyle changes combined with weight-reducing medications do not result in maintained weight loss.

title: R104 · Class I / Level B1 · Iron deficiency in HF
text: Intravenous iron supplementation is recommended in patients with symptomatic HFrEF and iron deficiency to alleviate HF symptoms and improve QoL.

title: R105 · Class IIa / Level B1 · Iron deficiency in HF
text: Intravenous iron supplementation should be considered in patients with symptomatic HFrEF and iron deficiency to reduce the risk of HFH.

title: R106 · Class IIb / Level C · Lung disease & sleep-disordered breathing
text: Adaptive servo-ventilation may be considered in patients with HFrEF and sleep-disordered breathing with predominant obstructive sleep apnoea to improve sleep quality, health-related QoL and symptoms.

title: R107 · Class III / Level A · Lung disease & sleep-disordered breathing
text: Adaptive servo-ventilation is not recommended in patients with HFrEF and sleep-disordered breathing with predominant central sleep apnoea because of an increased risk of CV and all-cause death.

title: R108 · Class IIa / Level C · Anxiety, depression & frailty
text: Assessment of anxiety, depression and frailty should be considered in patients with HF to support the development of personalized care plans and to identify factors that may contribute to adverse outcomes.

title: R109 · Class IIa / Level C · Other non-CV comorbidities
text: Influenza and pneumococcal vaccination should be considered in patients with HF to reduce the risk of pneumonia complications, hospitalization, and death.

title: R110 · Class III / Level B2 · Other non-CV comorbidities
text: NSAIDs and COX-2 inhibitors are not recommended in patients with HF as they increase the risk of HF worsening and HFH.

title: R111 · Class I / Level B1 · Multidisciplinary management
text: A multidisciplinary HF management programme is recommended in patients with HF to reduce the risk of HFH and death.

title: R112 · Class I / Level A · Multidisciplinary management
text: HF education and self-management strategies in patients with HF are recommended to reduce the risk of HFH or death.

title: R113 · Class I / Level B2 · Multidisciplinary management
text: Multidisciplinary interventions to improve adherence, including assessment of health literacy and polypharmacy review, are recommended in patients with HF to reduce the risk of hospitalization and death.

title: R114 · Class I / Level B1 · Exercise training & cardiac rehabilitation
text: Personalized exercise training, in the context of multidisciplinary exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation, is recommended for all stable patients, unless there are specific contraindications, in order to improve exercise capacity and QoL, and reduce the risk of all-cause hospitalization.

title: R115 · Class I / Level B2 · Exercise training & cardiac rehabilitation
text: Personalized exercise training outside exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation is recommended for all stable patients on a long-term basis, unless there are specific contraindications, in order to improve exercise capacity and QoL, and reduce the risk of

title: R116 · Class I / Level B1 · Exercise training & cardiac rehabilitation
text: Cardiac rehabilitation is recommended in patients with an LVAD to improve functional capacity and QoL.

title: R117 · Class IIa / Level B1 · Exercise training & cardiac rehabilitation
text: Cardiac rehabilitation should be considered in patients with DHF, as soon as safely possible, to improve functional capacity and QoL.

title: R118 · Class IIa / Level B1 · Invasive & non-invasive telemonitoring
text: Remote haemodynamic monitoring of PA pressure should be considered in symptomatic patients with HF, NYHA class III, and an HFH in the past 12 months in order to reduce the risk of HFH.

title: R119 · Class IIb / Level B1 · Invasive & non-invasive telemonitoring
text: Non-invasive telemonitoring modalities may be considered for patients with HF in order to reduce the risk of HFH.

title: R120 · Class I / Level B1 · Long-term follow-up, advance care & palliative care
text: Proactive discussion regarding HF trajectory, goals of care, and advance care planning is recommended in patients with advanced HF to facilitate communication on end of life and QoL.

title: R121 · Class I / Level B2 · Long-term follow-up, advance care & palliative care
text: Access to an integrated HF palliative care multidisciplinary team is recommended for patients in an advanced HF stage to improve QoL and reduce symptom burden.

title: R122 · Class I / Level C · HF and pregnancy
text: Pre-conception care and counselling is recommended for patients with HF to facilitate decision-making surrounding HF treatments, pregnancy, contraception, pre-implantation genetic screening, and assisted reproductive therapies.

title: R123 · Class I / Level C · HF and pregnancy
text: In pregnant women with HFrEF, it is recommended that non-selective beta-blockers are switched to beta -selective blockers (metoprolol, bisoprolol) with close mother and foetus monitoring to reduce the risk of adverse foetal events and a lower birth weight.

title: R124 · Class III / Level C · HF and pregnancy
text: ACE-Is, ARBs, ARNIs, MRAs, ivabradine, and SGLT2-Is are not recommended during pregnancy due to the risk of foetotoxicity or teratogenicity.

title: R125 · Class I / Level A · Cardiac amyloidosis
text: Treatment with a TTR silencer (vutrisiran) or stabilizer (tafamidis or acoramidis) for patients with variant or wild-type transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and NYHA classes I–III is recommended to reduce progression of symptoms and the risk of CV hospitalization and all-cause death.

title: Drug: Captopril
text: Captopril. ACE inhibitors. First class of drugs shown to reduce mortality and morbidity and improve symptoms in HFrEF; recommended in all patients with HFrEF unless contraindicated or not tolerated, uptitrated to the highest recommended dose (intermediate doses if target not tolerated). Target dose derived from post-MI trials Give with caution if SBP <100 mmHg, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m², or K⁺ >5.2 mEq/L Avoid abrupt withdrawal (clinical deterioration); if ARNI is not possible, continued ACE-I remains strongly advised Wash-out of at least 36 h before starting an ARNI (angio-oedema risk) Starting dose 6.25 mg t.i.d.; target dose 50 mg t.i.d..

title: Drug: Enalapril
text: Enalapril. ACE inhibitors. First class of drugs shown to reduce mortality and morbidity and improve symptoms in HFrEF; recommended in all patients with HFrEF unless contraindicated or not tolerated, uptitrated to the highest recommended dose (intermediate doses if target not tolerated). Comparator in PARADIGM-HF (ARNI reduced CV death/HFH by 20% vs enalapril) Give with caution if SBP <100 mmHg, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m², or K⁺ >5.2 mEq/L Avoid abrupt withdrawal (clinical deterioration); if ARNI is not possible, continued ACE-I remains strongly advised Wash-out of at least 36 h before starting an ARNI (angio-oedema risk) Starting dose 2.5 mg b.i.d.; target dose 10–20 mg b.i.d..

title: Drug: Lisinopril
text: Lisinopril. ACE inhibitors. First class of drugs shown to reduce mortality and morbidity and improve symptoms in HFrEF; recommended in all patients with HFrEF unless contraindicated or not tolerated, uptitrated to the highest recommended dose (intermediate doses if target not tolerated). Higher dose reduces morbidity/mortality vs lower dose, but no substantive placebo-controlled trial; optimal dose uncertain Give with caution if SBP <100 mmHg, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m², or K⁺ >5.2 mEq/L Avoid abrupt withdrawal (clinical deterioration); if ARNI is not possible, continued ACE-I remains strongly advised Wash-out of at least 36 h before starting an ARNI (angio-oedema risk) Starting dose 2.5–5 mg o.d.; target dose 20–35 mg o.d..

title: Drug: Ramipril
text: Ramipril. ACE inhibitors. First class of drugs shown to reduce mortality and morbidity and improve symptoms in HFrEF; recommended in all patients with HFrEF unless contraindicated or not tolerated, uptitrated to the highest recommended dose (intermediate doses if target not tolerated). Give with caution if SBP <100 mmHg, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m², or K⁺ >5.2 mEq/L Avoid abrupt withdrawal (clinical deterioration); if ARNI is not possible, continued ACE-I remains strongly advised Wash-out of at least 36 h before starting an ARNI (angio-oedema risk) Starting dose 1.25–2.5 mg b.i.d.; target dose 5 mg b.i.d..

title: Drug: Trandolapril
text: Trandolapril. ACE inhibitors. First class of drugs shown to reduce mortality and morbidity and improve symptoms in HFrEF; recommended in all patients with HFrEF unless contraindicated or not tolerated, uptitrated to the highest recommended dose (intermediate doses if target not tolerated). Target dose derived from post-MI trials PEACE subgroup: mortality reduction in LVEF 40–50% Give with caution if SBP <100 mmHg, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m², or K⁺ >5.2 mEq/L Avoid abrupt withdrawal (clinical deterioration); if ARNI is not possible, continued ACE-I remains strongly advised Wash-out of at least 36 h before starting an ARNI (angio-oedema risk) Starting dose 0.5 mg o.d.; target dose 4 mg o.d..

title: Drug: Sacubitril–valsartan (ARNI)
text: Sacubitril–valsartan (ARNI). ARNI. Angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitor. In PARADIGM-HF it reduced CV death or HFH by 20% vs enalapril, with better QoL, slower eGFR decline, lower loop-diuretic dose and lower hyperkalaemia risk. Patients tolerating an ACE-I/ARB with persistent symptoms should be switched; may also be used de novo. Optional lower start 24/26 mg b.i.d. for history of symptomatic hypotension, ACE-I-naïve patients, or eGFR 30–60 mL/min/1.73 m² HFpEF: PARAGON-HF missed its primary endpoint; benefit seen with LVEF below ~60–65%, so ARNI may be considered, especially at lower LVEF Pre- and post-discharge initiation showed similar efficacy/safety with larger NT-proBNP reduction vs ACE-I More frequent symptomatic hypotension Wash-out ≥36 h after ACE-I Same caution thresholds as ACE-I (SBP <100, eGFR <30, K⁺ >5.2); avoid abrupt withdrawal Not recommended in pregnancy Starting dose 49/51 mg b.i.d.; target dose 97/103 mg b.i.d..

title: Drug: Candesartan
text: Candesartan. ARBs. Recommended in HFrEF for patients who cannot tolerate an ACE-I or ARNI. Much lower incidence of cough and angio-oedema than ACE-I (no kininase inhibition). No ARB has reduced all-cause mortality in any trial; combining with an ACE-I increases adverse effects. CHARM-Alternative: reduced CV death and HFH in ACE-I-intolerant patients CHARM-Preserved: primary endpoint neutral; fewer HFH in LVEF 40–49% (retrospective) Evidence limited at higher LVEF Starting dose 4 mg o.d.; target dose 32 mg o.d..

title: Drug: Losartan
text: Losartan. ARBs. Recommended in HFrEF for patients who cannot tolerate an ACE-I or ARNI. Much lower incidence of cough and angio-oedema than ACE-I (no kininase inhibition). No ARB has reduced all-cause mortality in any trial; combining with an ACE-I increases adverse effects. HEAAL: high-dose losartan reduced HFH vs low dose in ACE-I-intolerant patients Starting dose (12.5) 25–50 mg o.d.; target dose 150 mg o.d..

title: Drug: Valsartan
text: Valsartan. ARBs. Recommended in HFrEF for patients who cannot tolerate an ACE-I or ARNI. Much lower incidence of cough and angio-oedema than ACE-I (no kininase inhibition). No ARB has reduced all-cause mortality in any trial; combining with an ACE-I increases adverse effects. Val-HeFT: reduced HFH on top of usual therapy including ACE-I Starting dose 40 mg b.i.d.; target dose 160 mg b.i.d..

title: Drug: Bisoprolol
text: Bisoprolol. Beta-blockers. Reduce morbidity and mortality in HFrEF on top of ACE-I and diuretics. Start early in clinically stable patients at low dose and uptitrate gradually to the highest tolerated dose; continue long-term even if symptoms do not improve. Shown to reduce risk of death in HFrEF β1-selective: acceptable in pregnancy with HFrEF (switch from non-selective agents) Ensure euvolaemia before initiation In decompensated HF, initiate cautiously in hospital once haemodynamically stabilized Effect in HFrEF with AF is uncertain (no dedicated RCT), although useful for rate control Temporary discontinuation advised in severe haemodynamic instability Starting dose 1.25 mg o.d.; target dose 10 mg o.d..

title: Drug: Carvedilol
text: Carvedilol. Beta-blockers. Reduce morbidity and mortality in HFrEF on top of ACE-I and diuretics. Start early in clinically stable patients at low dose and uptitrate gradually to the highest tolerated dose; continue long-term even if symptoms do not improve. Shown to reduce risk of death in HFrEF Maximum 50 mg b.i.d. may be given to patients >85 kg (Table 11, footnote d) Ensure euvolaemia before initiation In decompensated HF, initiate cautiously in hospital once haemodynamically stabilized Effect in HFrEF with AF is uncertain (no dedicated RCT), although useful for rate control Temporary discontinuation advised in severe haemodynamic instability Starting dose 3.125 mg b.i.d.; target dose 25 mg b.i.d..

title: Drug: Metoprolol succinate (CR/XL)
text: Metoprolol succinate (CR/XL). Beta-blockers. Reduce morbidity and mortality in HFrEF on top of ACE-I and diuretics. Start early in clinically stable patients at low dose and uptitrate gradually to the highest tolerated dose; continue long-term even if symptoms do not improve. Sustained-release succinate shown to reduce risk of death in HFrEF β1-selective: acceptable in pregnancy with HFrEF Ensure euvolaemia before initiation In decompensated HF, initiate cautiously in hospital once haemodynamically stabilized Effect in HFrEF with AF is uncertain (no dedicated RCT), although useful for rate control Temporary discontinuation advised in severe haemodynamic instability Starting dose 12.5–25 mg o.d.; target dose 200 mg o.d..

title: Drug: Nebivolol
text: Nebivolol. Beta-blockers. Reduce morbidity and mortality in HFrEF on top of ACE-I and diuretics. Start early in clinically stable patients at low dose and uptitrate gradually to the highest tolerated dose; continue long-term even if symptoms do not improve. Only reduced the combined endpoint of all-cause mortality and CV hospitalization (not shown to reduce CV/all-cause death alone) Ensure euvolaemia before initiation In decompensated HF, initiate cautiously in hospital once haemodynamically stabilized Effect in HFrEF with AF is uncertain (no dedicated RCT), although useful for rate control Temporary discontinuation advised in severe haemodynamic instability Starting dose 1.25 mg o.d.; target dose 10 mg o.d..

title: Drug: Eplerenone
text: Eplerenone. MRAs (steroidal). Recommended in all symptomatic HF regardless of LVEF (steroidal MRA for HFrEF; steroidal or non-steroidal MRA for HFpEF); reduce HFH or CV death. Mortality reduction demonstrated in HFrEF only. Eplerenone and finerenone are more receptor-specific and cause less gynaecomastia. Studied only in HFrEF (LVEF up to 35%) Class I (B1) after MI with LVEF ≤40% and signs of HF or diabetes Not tested at eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73 m²; use caution when K⁺ ≥5.0 mmol/L If K⁺ >5.5 mEq/L: recheck, then consider dose reduction or temporary discontinuation; restart when hyperkalaemia resolves Severe hyperkalaemia (K⁺ >5.5 or >6 mmol/L) → temporary down-titration/discontinuation of MRA and/or ACE-I/ARB/ARNI Not recommended in pregnancy Starting dose 25 mg o.d.; target dose 50 mg o.d..

title: Drug: Spironolactone
text: Spironolactone. MRAs (steroidal). Recommended in all symptomatic HF regardless of LVEF (steroidal MRA for HFrEF; steroidal or non-steroidal MRA for HFpEF); reduce HFH or CV death. Mortality reduction demonstrated in HFrEF only. Eplerenone and finerenone are more receptor-specific and cause less gynaecomastia. Optional 12.5 mg start where kidney status or hyperkalaemia warrant caution Studied across LVEF ranges; TOPCAT overall neutral, but meta-analysis with FINEARTS-HF positive for LVEF >40% Not tested at eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73 m²; use caution when K⁺ ≥5.0 mmol/L If K⁺ >5.5 mEq/L: recheck, then consider dose reduction or temporary discontinuation; restart when hyperkalaemia resolves Severe hyperkalaemia (K⁺ >5.5 or >6 mmol/L) → temporary down-titration/discontinuation of MRA and/or ACE-I/ARB/ARNI Not recommended in pregnancy Starting dose 12.5–25 mg o.d.; target dose 50 mg o.d..

title: Drug: Finerenone
text: Finerenone. MRAs (non-steroidal). Non-steroidal MRA studied in patients with LVEF >40% (FINEARTS-HF reduced HFH + CV death). Also recommended to reduce HF risk in T2DM with CKD (prevention). Start/target dose depends on eGFR (Table 11 footnote g) Not tested at eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73 m²; use caution when K⁺ ≥5.0 mmol/L If K⁺ >5.5 mEq/L: recheck, then consider dose reduction or temporary discontinuation; restart when hyperkalaemia resolves Severe hyperkalaemia (K⁺ >5.5 or >6 mmol/L) → temporary down-titration/discontinuation of MRA and/or ACE-I/ARB/ARNI Not recommended in pregnancy Starting dose 10 mg (eGFR ≤60) / 20 mg (eGFR >60) o.d.; target dose 20 mg (eGFR ≤60) / 40 mg (eGFR >60) o.d..

title: Drug: Dapagliflozin
text: Dapagliflozin. SGLT2 inhibitors. Recommended in all symptomatic HF regardless of LVEF to reduce HFH or CV death; also improve QoL. CV mortality reduction only in HFrEF (in HFpEF benefit driven by fewer HFH). Initiate in hospital after stabilization in decompensated HF. Common side effects: genital and urinary tract infections Mild initial eGFR decline expected; long-term kidney function improved Starting dose 10 mg o.d.; target dose 10 mg o.d..

title: Drug: Empagliflozin
text: Empagliflozin. SGLT2 inhibitors. Recommended in all symptomatic HF regardless of LVEF to reduce HFH or CV death; also improve QoL. CV mortality reduction only in HFrEF (in HFpEF benefit driven by fewer HFH). Initiate in hospital after stabilization in decompensated HF. Common side effects: genital and urinary tract infections Mild initial eGFR decline expected; long-term kidney function improved Starting dose 10 mg o.d.; target dose 10 mg o.d..

title: Drug: Loop diuretics
text: Loop diuretics. Diuretics. Recommended to relieve congestion in HF with volume overload; dynamic, individualized dosing guided by volume status (Class I A). Use the lowest dose that maintains euvolaemia; needs fall with optimal FMT/GDIT. Effects on morbidity/mortality not studied in adequately powered RCTs. Best strategy: multiparameter assessment (clinical at rest and dynamic manoeuvres, eGFR, electrolytes, natriuretic peptides ± imaging) In decompensated HF: IV loop diuretics for all patients with fluid overload (I A) Add short-term IV acetazolamide or oral hydrochlorothiazide if fluid overload persists on loop diuretics (IIa B1) Urinary Na⁺-guided diuretic therapy may be considered (IIb B1) Electrolyte disturbances, neurohormonal activation, kidney function decline, symptomatic hypotension Avoid chronic thiazide use in stable patients (severe, undetected electrolyte disturbances)

title: Drug: Potassium binders (patiromer, sodium zirconium cyclosilicate)
text: Potassium binders (patiromer, sodium zirconium cyclosilicate). Other. Gastrointestinal K⁺ binders can treat/prevent hyperkalaemia and facilitate continuation/uptitration of ACE-I/ARNI/ARB and MRA. No specific recommendation in the guideline: clinical-outcome benefit unproven. REALIZE-K: signal towards more HF deterioration with sodium zirconium cyclosilicate vs placebo (not powered for outcomes) GI symptoms; hypomagnesaemia (patiromer); oedema (sodium zirconium cyclosilicate)

title: Drug: Ivabradine
text: Ivabradine. If-channel inhibitor. Slows heart rate via If-current inhibition. Should be considered in symptomatic HFrEF, LVEF ≤35%, sinus rhythm, resting HR above 70 b.p.m., on highest tolerated FMT (IIa B1), or if beta-blocker not tolerated (IIa C). SHIFT: benefit driven mainly by fewer HFH. Initiate/uptitrate beta-blockers to target first, then reassess resting heart rate before adding ivabradine Not recommended in pregnancy Starting dose 5 mg b.i.d.; target dose 7.5 mg b.i.d..

title: Drug: Vericiguat
text: Vericiguat. sGC stimulator. Oral soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator; may be considered in symptomatic HFrEF with LVEF <45% despite optimal FMT (IIb B1). VICTORIA (recent worsening HF): lower CV death/HFH, no reduction in death. VICTOR (stable ambulatory, LVEF ≤40%): neutral on primary endpoint. Less benefit seen at the highest NT-proBNP levels in VICTORIA Starting dose 2.5 mg o.d.; target dose 10 mg o.d..

title: Drug: Hydralazine + isosorbide dinitrate
text: Hydralazine + isosorbide dinitrate. Vasodilators. Considered (IIa B2) in self-identified black patients with symptomatic HFrEF, LVEF ≤40%, on top of optimal FMT (reduced mortality and HFH, improved QoL in a small RCT). May be considered (IIb C) in HFrEF patients who cannot tolerate ACE-I, ARNI or ARB. Benefit in non-black patients unclear Older evidence (V-HeFT, male patients on digoxin + diuretics) underpins the intolerance recommendation Starting dose 37.5 mg/20 mg t.i.d.; target dose 75 mg/40 mg t.i.d..

title: Drug: Digoxin
text: Digoxin. Cardiac glycosides. Should be considered in symptomatic HFrEF with LVEF ≤40% despite optimal FMT to reduce HFH (IIa B1). DIG: neutral on mortality, fewer HFH. Also IIa C for AF rate control when beta-blockers are insufficient or not tolerated. Target serum concentration <1.2 ng/mL Eliminated mainly by the kidneys Narrow therapeutic window — careful monitoring Starting dose 62.5 µg o.d.; target dose 250 µg o.d. (titrate to plasma level).

title: Drug: Digitoxin
text: Digitoxin. Cardiac glycosides. DIGIT-HF (HFrEF, NYHA III/IV or LVEF ≤30% NYHA II): composite of all-cause death or HFH 39.5% vs 44.1% (HR 0.82); neither death nor HFH alone significant. Considered with digoxin as a cardiac glycoside (IIa B1). Target serum 10.5–23.6 nmol/L in DIGIT-HF Eliminated by hepatic metabolism Narrow therapeutic window — careful monitoring Starting dose 0.07 mg o.d.; target dose 0.1 mg o.d. (titrate to plasma level).

title: Drug: Omecamtiv mecarbil
text: Omecamtiv mecarbil. Cardiac myosin activator. GALACTIC-HF: modest reduction in HF events without a mortality benefit. Not currently approved for clinical use in HF.

title: Drug: Intravenous iron (iron deficiency)
text: Intravenous iron (iron deficiency). Comorbidity therapy. Recommended in symptomatic HFrEF with iron deficiency to alleviate symptoms and improve QoL (I B1); should be considered to reduce HFH (IIa B1). Iron status (TSAT, ferritin) is part of the initial laboratory work-up

title: Drug: Semaglutide / tirzepatide
text: Semaglutide / tirzepatide. Incretin-based therapy. Should be considered in symptomatic HF with LVEF ≥45% and BMI ≥30 kg/m², regardless of diabetes status, to reduce weight and improve exercise capacity and QoL (IIa B1). Prevention: GLP-1 RA in T2DM with another CV risk factor (IIa A).

title: Drug: Oral anticoagulants (DOACs, VKAs)
text: Oral anticoagulants (DOACs, VKAs). Antithrombotics. Oral anticoagulation is recommended in HF with clinical AF at elevated thromboembolic risk by CHA₂DS₂-VA (I A); DOACs preferred over VKAs (I B1). Patients with HCM and cardiac amyloidosis need anticoagulation irrespective of score.

title: Drug: AF rate/rhythm drugs (beta-blockers, digoxin, amiodarone)
text: AF rate/rhythm drugs (beta-blockers, digoxin, amiodarone). Antiarrhythmics. HFrEF with AF: beta-blockers first-line for rate control (I C); digoxin if rate remains high or beta-blockers not tolerated (IIa C); IV amiodarone or digoxin for acute rate control in haemodynamically unstable patients (IIb C). Urgent cardioversion if rapid rates with haemodynamic instability (I C).

title: Drug: Acute decompensated HF agents (oxygen, vasodilators, inotropes, vasopressors, opiates)
text: Acute decompensated HF agents (oxygen, vasodilators, inotropes, vasopressors, opiates). Acute care. Oxygen if SpO₂ <90% or PaO₂ <60 mmHg (I C). IV vasodilators may be considered if SBP >110 mmHg (IIb C). Inotropes may be considered if SBP <90 mmHg with hypoperfusion unresponsive to standard treatment (IIb C). Vasopressors, preferably norepinephrine, in cardiogenic shock (IIb C). Routine opiates not recommended (III C).

title: Drug: TTR-directed therapy (vutrisiran, tafamidis, acoramidis)
text: TTR-directed therapy (vutrisiran, tafamidis, acoramidis). Amyloidosis. TTR silencer (vutrisiran) or stabilizer (tafamidis or acoramidis) is recommended in variant or wild-type ATTR cardiac amyloidosis, NYHA I–III, to reduce symptom progression, CV hospitalization and death (I A).

title: Drug: Drugs to avoid or use with caution (NSAIDs/COX-2, pregnancy)
text: Drugs to avoid or use with caution (NSAIDs/COX-2, pregnancy). Avoid. NSAIDs and COX-2 inhibitors are not recommended (III B2) — they worsen HF and increase HFH. In pregnancy, ACE-I, ARB, ARNI, MRA, ivabradine and SGLT2-I are not recommended (foetotoxicity/teratogenicity); non-selective beta-blockers should be switched to β1-selective agents (metoprolol, bisoprolol). Glucose-lowering drugs without proven HF safety should be avoided in prevention.
